title: Psalms Bible Quiz - Chapter 9
description: Ten questions on Psalms 9: Yahweh's righteous judgment, the high tower for the oppressed and the nations caught in their own pit.

questions.text: With what does the psalmist say he will give thanks to Yahweh?
questions.explanation: Psalms 9:1 says he will give thanks to Yahweh with his whole heart and tell of all his marvelous works.

questions.text: Where does the psalmist say God sits as he judges righteously?
questions.explanation: Psalms 9:4 says God sits on the throne, judging righteously.

questions.text: According to verse 5, what has God blotted out forever and ever?
questions.explanation: Psalms 9:5 says God has destroyed the wicked and blotted out their name forever and ever.

questions.text: What will Yahweh be for the oppressed?
questions.explanation: Psalms 9:9 says Yahweh will be a high tower for the oppressed, a high tower in times of trouble.

questions.text: Who will put their trust in Yahweh, according to verse 10?
questions.explanation: Psalms 9:10 says those who know Yahweh's name will put their trust in him.

answers.text: Those who are strong in battle

questions.text: Where does verse 11 say Yahweh dwells?
questions.explanation: Psalms 9:11 calls for praises to Yahweh, who dwells in Zion.

questions.text: What does he who avenges blood not forget?
questions.explanation: Psalms 9:12 says he who avenges blood doesn't forget the cry of the afflicted.

questions.text: Where have the nations sunk down?
questions.explanation: Psalms 9:15 says the nations have sunk down in the pit that they made, and their own foot is taken in the net they hid.

answers.text: In the waters of the flood
In the mire of the streets
In the pit that they made

questions.text: According to verse 18, what shall not perish forever?
questions.explanation: Psalms 9:18 says the needy shall not always be forgotten, nor the hope of the poor perish forever.

questions.text: What does the psalmist ask Yahweh to let the nations know?
questions.explanation: Psalms 9:20 asks Yahweh to put the nations in fear and let them know that they are only men.
